question: Which official programs support older adults with limited retirement income?

answer.message:
These official programs may be relevant. The directory can guide further research; it doesn't determine whether someone qualifies.

District demographics can help identify relevant programs, but cannot establish individual eligibility. The agency must check current household, income, resource, residency and any age or disability requirements, as well as availability.

- **[Supplemental Security Income (SSI)](https://www.ssa.gov/ssi/text-eligibility-ussi.htm)** — Means-tested cash support. Limited countable income/resources; individual/couple unit, deeming/exclusions; U.S. residence and citizenship/qualified-status rules. 2026 general resource limits $2,000/$3,000; payment maximum is not an income cutoff. Application status: Application/appointment routes available; not a benefit guarantee.

- **[Medicare Part D Extra Help](https://www.ssa.gov/medicare/part-d-extra-help)** — Reduces prescription-drug coverage costs. Individual/spouse finances and countable-resource exclusions, Medicare/PartD status and applicable annual limits. Hawaiʻi income standard must be used. Application status: SSA states application can be made any time before/after PartD enrollment. Direct form redirected to a service message during research.

- **[Older Americans Act / EOA home and community services](https://health.hawaii.gov/eoa/home/home-and-community-services/)** — Nutrition, transport, personal care, case management and related supports. Service-specific assessment and county residence; not a universal cash-income entitlement. Household size/income may affect prioritization rather than categorical eligibility. Application status: County intake/referral; service capacity and waiting lists require confirmation.

Program sources were last checked **2026-10-26**. Eligibility rules in this directory remain incomplete; use the official links and confirm current requirements and application availability with the agency.
